label: late-episode drop at GO/D1, deeper when belief/last choice favour S2/a2
terms: (phase == GO) * belief_lo * np.exp(ep_trial/10.0) ;; (phase == D1) * belief_lo * np.exp(ep_trial/10.0) ;; (phase == GO) * np.exp(ep_trial/10.0) ;; (phase == D1) * np.exp(ep_trial/10.0) ;; (phase == GO) * table(prev_action, {1: 1, 2: -1}) * np.exp(ep_trial/10.0) ;; (phase == D1) * table(prev_action, {1: 1, 2: -1}) * np.exp(ep_trial/10.0) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) * np.exp(ep_trial/10.0) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) * table(prev_action, {1: 1, 2: -1}) * np.exp(ep_trial/10.0)
explanation: Raw GRU candidate n of unit 22 sits near +1 almost all the time. Timing explains R^2 0.86: it sags toward the end of the episode, mostly at GO (decile-9 mean 0.43), less at D1, barely at D2. Beyond timing, the sag is asymmetric and grows roughly exponentially with episode trial (exp(ep_trial/10)). It is deeper when the ideal-observer belief favours S2 (belief_lo < 0) and when the previous choice was a2, and shallower for S1 belief or a1. At GO, a rewarded previous trial deepens the drop further (the largest dips come in late streaks of rewarded a2 -> S2 common), and that reward effect is stronger after a2. D2 shows almost no history effect. Additive phase tables cap out at 0.18 (all) / 0.16 (all observed) because they miss the interaction with time-in-episode. With that interaction, observed-only terms reach dev R^2 0.43 and test 0.33 beyond timing. The within-decile time terms alone score only 0.01, so the belief/choice/reward x time interaction carries the gain. Not explained: individual late-episode windows, where the size of the dip still varies a lot. The dev-to-test drop shows the fit is sensitive to rare, extreme late-episode windows. No model outputs are used, and no comparison with the earlier value/policy explanation was scored here.
